# Read the brief

Most failed calls come from one rule that was skipped. Read every line of every file in
`input/`. Do not search by keyword instead of reading. Use only what the inputs say: never
copy a rule, value or sentence from anything else, and never guess a missing value.

## 1. Read
- Read each brief file from the first line to the last. If a file is long, read it in parts
  until you have seen every line.
- Read the tool API file: every tool, every request field, every allowed value, every response
  field. The tool names are fixed; fields and allowed values may differ from what you expect.

## 2. Resolve the documents (raw material)
The brief may be several documents: a mail, a policy extract, a memo, a code list.
- List each document with its date or order.
- A later memo or mail that changes a rule wins over the earlier document, unless it says it
  applies only to some cases. A code list defines allowed values and their meaning.
- Write every conflict and its winner, with both quotes, into `conflicts` in rules.json.

## 3. Write work/rules.json, the rule ledger
A list. One entry per atomic rule (one condition, one action):
    {"id": "R12", "quote": "<exact words from the brief>", "file": "<file name>",
     "kind": "<opening | who_is_on_line | third_party | identity | debt_statement | dates |
              amounts | persuasion | read_back | recording | special_case | closing |
              required_sentence | forbidden | other>",
     "rule": "<the rule in one plain sentence>",
     "implemented_by": ""}            filled in by the design step
- The quote must appear word for word in the file. The check step verifies this.
- Split compound rules. "Say X, ask nothing else, and close as Y" is three rules.
- Precedence ("this comes before rule N", "takes priority") is its own rule.
- Numbers, dates, limits, counts and exact sentences go in the rule, unchanged.

## 4. Write work/spec.json, the parameters
The exact keys are in builder/reference/SPEC.md (read it in full). Fill every field the inputs give; leave a field out when the inputs say nothing about it,
and add a `gaps` list naming each missing item. Never invent a value.
    call_variables        names and meaning of the variables every call starts with
    opening               the first sentence's required content; who to ask for and how
    forbidden_before_verification   words that must not be said before identity passes
    confirmation_words    what counts as confirming identity, and what does not
    identity              questions in order, the tool field values for each, answer
                          format per question (date / digits:N / year / text), numeric date
                          order, wrong-answer limit and what does not count as wrong
    calendar              business days, weekend days, holidays, how "Nth business day after
                          today" is counted, "this"/"next" weekday meaning
    bands                 per band: days-late range, deadline rule, persuasion attempts
    products              per product type: spoken name, floor field, any other rule
    persuasion            what each attempt proposes (amount and date)
    callback              window (days and hours, inclusive or not), retries allowed
    special_cases         each: trigger words, action, tool call, outcome/reason, precedence
    outcomes              the outcome table: outcome, reason, when
    notes                 when notes are written, reasons, when never to write them
    required_sentences    exact sentences, with when they must be said
    restricted_words      words the brief forbids in one situation and requires in another
                          (for example a word allowed only after a tool succeeded)
    tool_failures         what to do when each tool fails, and how many retries
    multi_product         ordering, one read-back or many, per-product counting
    tools                 per tool: the API fields to fill from call variables, and which the
                          agent fills

## 4b. Words with a condition
Look for every rule that allows a word or a claim only after something happens (for example
a claim allowed only after a tool succeeded). Put each such word in `restricted_words`. If a
required sentence (the opening, a fixed line) needs the same idea, write it in other words in
the spec, and note the paraphrase in rules.json. Keep the paraphrase plain and as close to the
original as possible, so a reader still recognises the required statement: prefer a related
form of the same word (a noun instead of a verb) over an unusual synonym. Never put such a word in a line spoken
before the condition can be true.

## 5. Check before moving on
- Every line of every brief file is covered by at least one rule or is plainly descriptive.
- Every rule with a number, date or sentence has it in spec.json too.
- `gaps` lists anything the design step must handle without a value. Prefer the safe
  behaviour: do less, record nothing uncertain, close honestly.

# Harbour Lane Bank - Arrears Contact Policy (extract), version 4

## 2. Opening
2.1 The first thing the assistant says: that it is an automated assistant phoning on behalf of Harbour Lane Bank, and that calls are monitored for quality.
2.2 Then: "Could I speak to {salutation} {surname}, please?"
2.3 Before the member has passed security, never mention arrears, balance, overdue, money owed, or any account type.
2.4 Confirmation means the person says yes or gives the member's name as their own. Anything else, ask once more; still unclear after that, end the contact with code NC-UNC.
2.5 If the number is not the member's: NC-WRG. If the member has passed away: say "Please accept my condolences." and end with NC-DEC, asking nothing else.
2.6 Third parties: say nothing about why you call. Offer a call-back on the next working day between 09:30 and 17:30. Book it if they agree a time in that window, then end with NC-CBK. If they cannot, end with NC-NCB.

## 3. Security
3.1 Two questions, in this order: the postcode on the account, then the member's year of birth.
3.2 Send the postcode exactly as said, the year of birth as four digits.
3.3 Two wrong answers in total end security. Then: direct the member to online banking and end with SEC-FAIL. Never state any arrears after a failed check.
3.4 A member who refuses to answer is told once that the questions keep their savings safe. A second refusal ends with SEC-REF.

## 4. Arrears and dates
4.1 After security, fetch the accounts and say, for each account, its name, the overdue sum and how many days overdue.
4.2 Working days are Monday to Friday except bank holidays: 2026-11-30, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28, 2027-01-01.
4.3 Bands by days overdue: 1-10 "light": latest promise date 10 working days after today, one persuasion attempt. 11-30 "medium": 6 working days, two attempts. 31-90 "heavy": 3 working days, two attempts.
4.4 A promise date must be a working day, not before today and not after the band's latest date.

## 5. Amounts and persuasion
5.1 Ask for the full overdue sum first. Never ask the member to name an amount.
5.2 The lowest acceptable amount is the account's min_due. Offer it once, only if the member says the full sum is too much, adding: "anything left stays in arrears."
5.3 Attempt 1: the full overdue sum (or min_due if already said too much) on the last working day of the current week; if today is that day, the last working day of next week. Attempt 2: min_due on the latest promise date.
5.4 When attempts are used up: end with code PTP-NO / REFUSED.

## 6. Recording and closing
6.1 Read every agreed promise back in one go and ask "Is that correct?"; record each promise only after a clear yes.
6.2 Only say a promise is in place after the system confirms it. If recording fails, try once more; if it fails again, say so and use PTP-NO / SYSERR.
6.3 After a recorded promise say: "We will send you a letter confirming this arrangement."
6.4 Illness, bereavement or redundancy: one sentence of sympathy, no persuasion, offer the Member Care team once (queue CARE). Accepted: transfer, XFER / CARE. Declined: PTP-NO / CARE-DECL.
6.5 Request for a lower monthly amount or a new plan: transfer to queue PLAN, XFER / PLAN.
6.6 Says already paid: tell them payments show within two working days, take no promise; PAID.
6.7 Disputes the account: do not argue, no promise; PTP-NO / DISPUTE.
6.8 Asks for a person: ask once if you can help; if they insist, queue DESK, XFER / DESK.
6.9 One end-contact call per conversation, the last action, after thanking the member and saying goodbye.
MEMO - Harbour Lane Bank, Collections Operations
From: Raj Okafor, Ops Manager
Date: 5 November 2026
Re: Changes to policy v4 for the automated pilot

With immediate effect, for the pilot only:

1. Security (3.3): three wrong answers in total end security, not two.
2. Call-backs (2.6): the window is 10:00 to 16:00, still the next working day only.

Everything else in v4 stands.

# Design the agent

## 1. Generate from the reference
    cp -r builder/reference work/reference
    python3 work/reference/generate.py work/spec.json input/<tool api file> work/workflow.json
The reference already does, generically: date facts from `now`; identity with answer
cleaning; third party and callback window; one to three products with per-product band,
deadline, floor and attempts; one read-back and one recording per product; notes only if
the spec uses them; special cases from the spec; a closing hook that sets the outcome from
what was actually recorded; retry caps on every failing tool.

## 2. Edit only what the spec cannot express
Go through work/rules.json. For each rule write in `implemented_by` where it lives: a node
name, a prompt line, a route, a code step or a hook. If a rule has no home, edit
work/reference (never builder/reference) to add one, then regenerate.

Hard rules for every edit (they come from failures we have seen):
1. A count in the brief ("once", "at most twice", a number of attempts) lives in a route,
   a variable or a fixed spoken line, never only in a prompt.
2. A new route must yield to every rule the brief says comes first: extract each
   higher-priority trigger and exclude it from the route.
3. A word the brief forbids in one situation must not appear in any fixed spoken line
   that can be said in that situation, even if another rule requires the idea. Paraphrase.
4. Every tool that can fail has a capped retry and an exit that still closes the call.
5. A rambling, cut-off or nonsense reply is never an answer or a refusal; the agent replies
   with a neutral line and never repeats an offer because of it.
6. Arithmetic, dates and counting happen in code. The model gets finished facts.
7. Tools exist only in the nodes where the brief allows them. Nothing about the account
   is in any prompt or line the model sees before verification.
8. Required sentences are copied word for word from the brief.
9. Code in code steps and hooks never raises and never contains a double brace.

## 3. Regenerate and hand over
    python3 work/reference/generate.py work/spec.json input/<tool api file> work/workflow.json
Then use check-agent. If a check fails, fix the spec or the generator copy, never the
workflow JSON by hand.
